sentences.text: S1 stated that the purpose of the meeting is to hear the client's instructions regarding protection from her ex-partner and to explain legal options.
S2 stated she attended by bus because parking was difficult.
S2 stated her ex-partner is Ryan Hale.
S2 stated they were together for six years and split up in August.
S2 stated Ryan moved out to his brother's house after the split.
S2 stated she still lives at 9 Calder Court, which is a tenancy in her name only.
S2 stated her daughter is Mia, who is four years old and attends nursery.
S2 stated Ryan was Mia's father and used to see her on Sundays, but she stopped this contact after October.
S2 stated Ryan has come to her flat every weekend (Friday or Saturday night) since August, banging on the door and shouting through the letterbox.
S2 stated Ryan was away for one weekend when she did not hear him.
S2 disclosed that on the twelfth of October, Ryan put his hands around her neck in her hallway while she was giving him Mia's bag, pushing her against the wall until she could not.
S2 stated Mia was asleep in her room during the incident on the twelfth of October.
S2 stated her neighbour called the police after hearing her screaming, and the police arrested Ryan.
S2 stated Ryan was released on bail, but the bail ran out and he is now released under investigation with no current bail conditions.
S2 stated that on the twentieth of October, Ryan turned up, grabbed her phone, and smashed it on the floor.
S2 stated she told the officer on the case about the phone being smashed, and the phone cost about two hundred pounds.
S2 stated Ryan sent her a text on the third of November threatening to kill her, and she screenshotted the message.
S2 stated Ryan sent her voice notes saying she would regret it.
S2 stated her friend Gemma told her that Ryan keeps a knife in his van for work.
S2 stated she has never seen a knife in Ryan's van herself; this information is second-hand from Gemma.
S2 stated Ryan is on the birth certificate for Mia, meaning he has parental responsibility.
S2 stated she works part-time at a pharmacy for about eighteen hours and receives universal credit.
S2 stated she has a crime reference number on her phone (H R one four) which she will send to S1.
S2 stated she went to the GP two days after the twelfth of October, and the doctor recorded marks on her neck.
S2 stated her priority is for Ryan to stop coming to the flat and stop messaging her.
S2 stated she does not want Mia to see Ryan until the situation is sorted.
S1 advised that an application for a non-molestation order would be appropriate to forbid Ryan from using or threatening violence, contacting her, and coming within a set distance.
S1 advised that the court could make the non-molestation order without notice given the strangulation and threat to kill, allowing Ryan a chance to respond at a return hearing.
S1 advised that breaching a non-molestation order is a criminal offence and she should call the police immediately if it happens.
S1 stated that a non-molestation order would not stop Ryan from applying for contact, but any contact would be dealt with separately and the court would be aware of the abuse.
